newsitem.title: POLAND: World oil giants interested in Polish sell-off.
newsitem.headline: World oil giants interested in Polish sell-off.

text.p: Thirteen firms have signalled interest in stakes of Poland's two largest refineries under the government's scheme to privatise the oil sector, the state-owned holding group overseeing the programme said on Wednesday.

The group said the firms interested in stakes of Petrochemia Plock SA and Rafineria Gdanska SA were Italy's Agip Petroli, British Petroleum, U.S. Conoco, French Elf, Exxon, Koch Industries International, Russia's Lukoil, Kuwait's Maroil, Finland's Neste, Royal Dutch/Shell, Norway's Statoil, Texaco and Total.
The group, Nafta Polska SA, said in a statement that these companies bought the second part of the memorandum, which contains more details about the sector and terms of its privatisation.
The sale of refineries' stakes is widely expected next year after Nafta launches a final tender for them. It first needs to select a firm advising it on the privatisation.

Under the government's scheme, Nafta will offer up to 30 percent of shares in the refineries. The buyers would be allowed to increase their stakes to more than 50 percent after investing in the modernisation of the companies.
As an incentive, the investors would also gain access to state-owned petrol station network CPN SA.
But the incorporation of CPN into Nafta, which would enable such access for investors, is being delayed by protests within CPN, which would prefer to be privatised separately.
